hpi: 83-year-old woman brought in with abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting that began 1 hour before arrival. imaging.text: Non-contrast: no bowel wall thickening, clear mesentery, fluid within small bowel loops, no free fluid. Contrast phase: reduced mural enhancement of the distal jejunum, the ileum and the right colon. CT angiography: intraluminal filling defect in the superior mesenteric artery about 6.5 cm from its origin, with non-opacification of its distal branches (middle colic, right colic, ileocolic, jejunal and ileal arteries). No free intraperitoneal gas. Appendix normal. Pancreas normal without peripancreatic fluid. IMPRESSION: acute superior mesenteric artery embolism with ischaemia of the small bowel and right colon.

meta.note: First emergency visit of the same patient as CR27. Leucocytosis (value not given). Discharged on oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole.

label: diverticulitis
hpi: 58-year-old man with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and uncomplicated diverticulitis two years ago, who was seen here two days ago with a week of left lower quadrant pain, diagnosed with uncomplicated diverticulitis on CT and sent home on oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. He returns with worsening left lower quadrant pain.
physical_exam: Examination findings at this visit are not reported in the source.

imaging.exam_name: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast (two days ago)
imaging.text: Wall thickening and pericolic fat stranding of the sigmoid colon. IMPRESSION: uncomplicated diverticulitis.

imaging.exam_name: CT abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast (today)
imaging.text: Sigmoid wall thickening and fat stranding with a new encapsulated fluid collection, consistent with abscess. Dilated proximal small bowel with decompressed distal small bowel and a transition point near the abscess. IMPRESSION: complicated diverticulitis with abscess and small bowel obstruction.

source.authors: Walter FA, Rimkus G.
source.title: Complicated Diverticulitis With Associated Small Bowel Obstruction: A Case Report.

meta.stage: WSES stage 1b-2a: diverticular abscess with small bowel obstruction (return visit 2 days later)
meta.note: Return visit of the patient in CR26. Laparotomy: sigmoid inflammatory mass adherent to small bowel; sigmoid resection.

label: diverticulitis
hpi: 69-year-old man with 6 days of dizziness, mild right upper quadrant pain and rigors. No urinary, gastrointestinal or respiratory symptoms. Past history: glaucoma only.
physical_exam: Afebrile. Abdomen soft and not distended. Lung fields clear.

microbiology.result: Streptococcus species and Bacteroides species isolated.

imaging.text: Normal gallbladder without stones. No intra- or extrahepatic biliary dilatation. Liver smooth with regular echotexture; normal flow in the main portal vein. Appendix, pancreas, spleen and kidneys normal.

imaging.exam_name: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast (later in the week)
imaging.text: Normal biliary tree. Acute sigmoid diverticulitis with tiny locules of extramural gas (localised perforation) without abscess, with stranding of the peritoneal reflection, sigmoid mesentery and left iliac fossa. Linear filling defects of thrombus in the inferior mesenteric vein to its confluence with the splenic vein; further thrombus with gas locules in the main portal and splenic veins. IMPRESSION: perforated sigmoid diverticulitis complicated by pylephlebitis.

source.authors: Wali L, Shah A, Sleiman S, Hogsand T, Humphries S.
source.title: Acute pylephlebitis secondary to perforated sigmoid diverticulitis: A case report.

meta.stage: WSES stage 1a: localised perforation with septic thrombophlebitis of the portal system (pylephlebitis)
meta.note: Inflammatory markers raised and liver tests mildly cholestatic (values not given); initially treated as ascending cholangitis.

label: diverticulitis
hpi: 84-year-old woman with worsening left lower quadrant abdominal pain for 2 days, nausea and reduced appetite, like her previous episodes of diverticulitis. No fever, chills, diarrhoea, urinary symptoms, chest pain or breathlessness; last bowel movement yesterday. Past history: hypertension, reflux disease, diverticulitis, hip osteoarthritis, chronic back pain with an implanted spinal cord stimulator.
physical_exam: Vital signs normal; afebrile, non-toxic, not in distress. Abdomen soft with mild left lower quadrant tenderness and no peritonism.

imaging.exam_name: CT abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast
imaging.text: Thickened small bowel loop with surrounding inflammatory change and marked fat stranding, with a focus of gas in the adjacent mesentery suggesting focal perforation. IMPRESSION: focal small bowel perforation, likely of a diverticulum.

source.authors: Tapias E, Rivera EF, Finlayson B, Rowe DA, Mateja HL, Umbu LK, DeVito PM.
source.title: Perforated Jejunal Diverticulum Mimicking Diverticulitis: A Case Report of Acute Abdominal Pain in an Elderly Patient.

meta.stage: Perforated jejunal diverticulitis with mesenteric abscess (WSES-equivalent stage 1b)
meta.note: Other labs unremarkable (values not given); an inflammatory marker reported as 38 mm/hr (unit inconsistent; omitted). Laparotomy: perforated jejunal diverticulum 60 cm from the ligament of Treitz with a small mesenteric abscess. Labelled diverticulitis, as the CDM label covers diverticular disease of any segment (ICD K57).

label: pancreatitis
hpi: 37-year-old man with insulin-dependent diabetes, congenital clubfoot and several past operations, with epigastric pain for a few days, now radiating to the back: dull, constant, worse with eating and drinking, not relieved by over-the-counter analgesics; nausea and vomiting. No fever; normal bowel movements. Medications: atorvastatin, pantoprazole, insulin glargine and lispro, and weekly dulaglutide, increased from 0.75 to 1.5 mg two weeks ago, after which he had severe nausea and vomiting. Non-smoker, occasional alcohol, no drug use.
physical_exam: Examination findings are not reported in the source.

imaging.text: Peripancreatic fat stranding. IMPRESSION: acute pancreatitis.
No intrahepatic duct dilatation and no hepatic mass. Common bile duct 2 mm without stones. Gallbladder distended without evidence of acute cholecystitis.

source.authors: Khan AB, Shah A, Ahmad S, Khan MI, Amir A.
source.title: Dulaglutide (Trulicity)-Induced Acute Pancreatitis: A Case Report.

meta.stage: Revised Atlanta mild: interstitial oedematous pancreatitis without organ failure
meta.note: Serum alcohol < 3 (outside the catalogue). Lipase fell to 439 U/L by day 5.

label: cholecystitis
hpi: 68-year-old previously healthy woman in hospital for 10 days with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia (admitted after 6 days of fever, chest tightness and diarrhoea), who now develops constant right upper quadrant abdominal pain and a new fever of 38.3 C.
physical_exam: Temperature 38.3 C. Right upper quadrant tenderness with a positive Murphy sign. Coarse breath sounds in both lungs.

imaging.text: Distended gallbladder with wall thickening and biliary sludge; no gallstones. IMPRESSION: acute acalculous cholecystitis.

source.authors: Ying M, Lu B, Pan J, Lu G, Zhou S, Wang D, Li L, Shen J, Shu J, From the COVID-19 Investigating and Research Team.
source.title: COVID-19 with acute cholecystitis: a case report.

meta.stage: Tokyo 2018 grade I: acalculous cholecystitis without organ dysfunction or marked local inflammation
meta.note: On admission (10 days earlier): WBC 3.64 x10^9/L, neutrophils 70.7%, ALT 19, AST 27 U/L, bilirubin 19.9 umol/L, CRP 33.7 mg/L. Treated with percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage.

label: appendicitis
hpi: 32-year-old man without known illness with 2 days of insidious, progressive, constant pain in the left iliac fossa, not radiating, with nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite. No rectal bleeding, melaena or fever; normal bowel and bladder habits. No previous surgery. Another centre suspected diverticulitis.
physical_exam: Tachycardic. Tenderness, rebound tenderness and guarding in the left iliac fossa. Normal digital rectal examination.

imaging.text: Non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure in the left iliac fossa with surrounding echogenic mesentery and probe tenderness; no free fluid.

imaging.exam_name: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
imaging.text: Large bowel mainly on the left and small bowel mainly on the right; superior mesenteric artery to the right of the vein; no duodenum between the SMA and aorta (complete midgut non-rotation). Appendix arising from the caecum in the left iliac fossa, with a thickened wall, periappendiceal fat stranding and two appendicoliths (9 x 7 and 6 x 5 mm). IMPRESSION: acute appendicitis with intestinal malrotation.

source.authors: Kharel H, Pokhrel NB, Kharel Z, Sah D.
source.title: A Case Report on Left-sided Appendicitis with Intestinal Malrotation.

meta.stage: AAST grade 1 / WSES uncomplicated: left-sided appendicitis with intestinal malrotation
